query: In 2013, among advanced economies, exactly one had an unemployment rate above 26.8% (among the group with an official output-gap estimate). How much of that economy's unemployment rate was cyclical, in percentage points, signed (positive if above the sustainable level)? Convention: take the WEO output-gap estimate and assume that each 1% of output gap moves the unemployment rate by one-half percentage point in the opposite direction.

text.text: Identifies the relationship between the output gap and the deviation of unemployment from its natural rate (Okun's law, coefficient about -1/2).
text.accept: full = names Okun's law / output-gap-to-unemployment-gap link with coefficient near 0.5; no = simple regression only

computation.text: Cyclical unemployment of the identified economy (GRC) in 2013 = 9.14 pp
computation.accept: full = within tolerance; correct country identification required (hidden)

provenance.selection: seeded draw (20261030), distinct country within style where possible

gold_report_note: No corpus report states these values; gold is recomputed from the frozen WEO vintage by formula (formula-validated, no published figure).
distractors: potential-output estimation by HP filter alone
predicate: among the 27 economies with a published WEO output gap, unemployment rate (LUR) > 26.8 in 2013
